_comment: The COMPLETE list of surfaces allowed to run with minUnlockTier 'any_authenticated' — usable by a signed-in member who has NOT been approved in Unlock. Unlock approval is what grants access to this app: every other surface requires it, and a new one should use the 'approved_full' default. Enforced by ctf/scripts/check-unlock-tier-exceptions.mjs; CI fails on any call site missing here, and on any entry that has stopped using the bypass, so the list can only shrink on its own. kind 'machinery' = the Unlock gate cannot function if this is gated (the flow itself, the account area, bug reporting, small feeds a gated screen needs to render). kind 'exception' = a real capability deliberately opened to unapproved members by a dated owner decision, and every one needs 'feature' and 'decision'. There are six such features, named below; the sixth, '3.1 open sign-up use' (owner decision, 2026-10-27), covers the 'signed_in' and 'signed_in_posting' tiers. ADDING ANOTHER IS THE OWNER'S DECISION, NEVER A BUILD STEP — ask first; the answer for a new surface is almost always 'approved_full'.

exceptions.reason: The Unlock flow itself. A member with no tier yet has to be able to reach the thing that grants one.
Unlock submission and status routes — same reason as the page above.
Your own account screen. Nobody may be locked out of seeing or deleting their own data by a tier.
Your own block list; same posture as the rest of the account area.
Your own data export and deletion screen.
Account, profile, and deletion routes behind the account area.
Filing a problem report. The member most likely to hit a bug is the one stuck in onboarding, and gating this would silence exactly them.
The one-time notice state for a screen a not-yet-approved member can already see.
The currency options feed for a dropdown on a gated screen. Reads a global catalog, not anyone's data.

Knowledge library contribution (owner decision, 2026-07-29). Contributing is a route INTO verification: judging a contribution means looking at a real person writing real things, which is the same look Unlock asks for.
The routes behind the knowledge library contribution above.
Contributions is open to any signed-in member; a fundraiser nobody may reach raises nothing.
The routes behind the Contributions screen above.

Quora account deletion survey (owner decision, 2026-08-19). The research is about people outside this app, so approval cannot be the bar without sampling only the members already reached; sign-in keeps bulk junk out and is not a claim that the member is verified.
The submit route behind the survey above.

Writing a comment or leaving a reaction under a blog post, by a signed-in member who is not yet approved. Same reasoning as the Knowledge Library contribution exception: judging what somebody wrote is the same look Unlock asks for, so gating it would review the same account twice. Nothing an unapproved member writes is publicly visible — visibility is decided per person by lib/fireside/visibility.ts, and approval makes everything they have written appear at once. Reading needs no account at all and no gate, so it is not on this list.

The Fireside PAGE, under the same exception decided for its API on 2026-09-13, and only for that one slug — pluginPageMinUnlockTier in lib/plugins/repository.ts returns 'approved_full' for every other plugin. The API already ran at 'any_authenticated' while the page did not, so a member who followed a link from a blog post to join a conversation met a 'finish verifying' wall instead of the comment box, which is the opposite of what the exception was decided for: writing here is a route INTO verification. Nothing an unapproved member writes is publicly visible.

Reading the invitations to people listed in the Directory, in full, by any signed-in account. The invites are how people arrive from Quora, and seeing who has been invited is the reason to make an account. Reading needs a sign-in so the list is not public, which is why the invites left the blog; approval is not required because the people reading are mostly the people invited. Only the invite wall reads this gate: its page at /apps/directory/invites and its API routes (GET /api/directory/invites and GET /api/directory/invites/[slug]/image). The Directory itself, its search and every listing still need full approval. The invitations already published on the blog before 2026-10-15 are marked public and readable signed out, picture included; that part needs no account at all, so it is not part of this exception.

Today, the 3.1 home read, at 'signed_in'. Reading stays open to every signed-in member, after the 14 days too (owner-approved plan ctf/docs/developer/SOCIAL_REDESIGN_3_1_PLAN.md, Access). Account restrictions still apply.

requireSocketRelayPostAccess at 'signed_in_posting', used only by POST /api/socket-relay/requests: posting an ask from + New. Open while approved, inside the first 14 days, or waiting on an address; pauses after day 14 until Unlock is done. Every other SocketRelay route stays approved-only.
Mood at 'signed_in': a member's own check-in, open to every signed-in member and after the 14 days.
ClickLog at 'signed_in': a member's private log, open to every signed-in member and after the 14 days. The owner trends surface keeps its admin check.
What Works member gate at 'signed_in': reading, suggesting, endorsing and proposing problems. The admin gate in the same file is unchanged.
A member's own notifications, shown as Activity in 3.1, at 'signed_in' (was support_only).

requireChymeMemberRoomAccess at 'signed_in' for the Main Room only: reading the room, joining as a listener, the heartbeat and leaving. A member not yet approved joins with the listener role and sees no raise-hand or speaker controls; speaking, chat, every other room and the admin routes stay approved-only (owner-approved plan ctf/docs/developer/SOCIAL_REDESIGN_3_1_PLAN.md, Access; confirmed by the owner 2026-10-28).
